keywords: Epidemiology, health
abstract: PADI-web (Platform for Automated extraction of Disease Information from the web) is an automated biosurveillance system dedicated to the monitoring of online news sources for the detection of animal health infectious events.  PADI-web automatically collects news with customised queries, classifies them and extracts epidemiological information (diseases, dates, symptoms, hosts and locations). In order to identify relevant news with PADI-web, specific models using machine learning approaches and labeled data have been integrated for monitoring plant diseases (e.g. Xylella fastidiosa). A limited version is available with free access for research or web monitoring. We warmly invite you to cite the project (cf. Publications). To get access to advanced functionalities and the extended data, please do not hesitate to contact us at padi-web@cirad.fr.

They mainly consist of georeferenced prospecting data in citrus plots (all Reunion data and most of the other two territories), as well as in nurseries and private individuals (only Guadeloupe and Martinique for these two types of sites). keywords: Epidemiology, risk, plant health, Xylella fastidiosa, xf, XYLEFA
abstract: The data relate to temporal and spatial monitoring of the bacterium Xylella fastidiosa in France from 2015 to the present day. This bacterium, a quarantine organism on the territory of the European Union, is transmitted by biting-sucking insects and attacks a wide range of host plants (tree crops, wine cultures, ornamental crops, perfume plants, aromatic and medicinal plants). It was detected in Corsica and PACA regions in 2015 and then in Occitanie in 2020. Each year, an official surveillance is omplement on national territory, in accordance with European regulations (executing regulation (EU) 2020/1201), and thousands of plants are sampled and then analyzed in the laboratory to search for the bacteria and identify its subspecies if necessary. These data centralized by ANSES come from various field structures (SRALs, FREDONs, etc.), form the network of approved laboratories and the national reference laboratory. The EPPO and INSEE repositories are used to inform the plant species and the location data of the plants sampled (INSEE codes), respectively. Three files are made available, the data set resulting from the monitoring of the bacterium (data_XF_****-**-**), a table of attributes describing the variables used (tableau_attributs_XF) and the spatial grid (500m x 500m) which allowed the construction of the dataset (grid_quadrat_XF).

keywords: Epidemiology, risk, plant health, Grapevine flavescence dorée phytoplasma,PHYP64
abstract: Flavescence dorée (FD) survey data is centralized in a GIS database on the information system of the ESV Platform (French Epidemiological Plant Health Surveillance Platform). This database is in postgresql with the PostGIS extension. Flavescence dorée is caused by a phytoplasma that multiplies in the vessels of the vine. This phytoplasma is dispersed by a leafhopper Scaphoideus titanus that feeds of the sap of the vines. As the FD phytoplasma is classified as a quarantine organism within the EU, compulsory control of the disease has been implemented in the wine-growing regions. In particular, it involves monitoring of the vineyards in order to detect the symptoms of grapevine yellows. Infection by FD phytoplasma is then confirmed and distinguished from infection by bois noir (BN) phytoplasma by sampling followed by PCR analyses in approved laboratories. These data relate to 9124 vineyard plots over the years from 2012 to 2021 for the Auvergne-Rhône-Alpes region (Savoie’s vineyards in the departments of Haute-Savoie, Ain and Savoie) and 91847 vineyard plots over the years from 2013 to 2020 for the Bourgogne-Franche-Comté region (in the Côte d'Or and Saône-et-Loire departments). The information collected in this dataset, respectively by FREDON Auvergne-Rhône-Alpes and FREDON Bourgogne-Franche-Comté, are: distinct code of the sample, date of the sample, identifier of the commune, number of vine stocks sampled, result of the molecular  for FD and/or BN phytoplasma infection, the geographical coordinates of the sample (longitude and latitude) and sometimes grapevine variety (or its color : green, black).

The Casier Viticole Informatisé (CVI) is a database compiled by customs from the declarations of winegrowers and wineries. It centralizes the characteristics of grapevine plots of the French vineyard. The owner of this annual data set is the Comité National des Interprofessions des Vins à appellation d'origine et à indication géographique (CNIV). Information on vineyard parcels is available for each cadastral parcel (whose polygons are available from the French land registry). Each cadastral parcel is sometimes divided into several sub-cropping plots, which are not associated with specific polygons.The information available for each sub-cropping plots :year of planting, grapevine variety, Controlled Origin Certification, anonymous farm identifier, total and cultivated surface area.

titre: Land use map of Burgundy and Savoy vineyards
web-access: (Access to data @ https://doi.org/10.57745/3R8F9P, Illustration Riley Luke INRAE @ https://forgemia.inra.fr/beyond/beyond-vre/dataflow-beyond/-/raw/master/img/vineyards.png)
abstract: The land cover map provided was constructed from several data sources. This mapping used data from the Casier Viticole Informatisé (CVI) of 2014 for Bourgogne region and of 2020 for Savoie region as primary data for the grapevine occupation layer. The IGN databases were used for the urban layer (BDTopo) and for the forest layer (BDForêtV2). Data from the Registre Parcellaire Graphique (RPG) were used for mainly non-vine crops and finally data from the CESBIO OSO layer (2018) for water and road classes. The final layer was produced following a series of processing under the softwares R and QGIS. Two "raster" files in GeoTiff format (resolution of 10 meters) respectively cover the vineyard of Burgundy (departments of Côte d'Or and Saône-et-Loire) and of Savoy (all or part of the departments of Haute-Savoie, of Ain and Savoie).

abstract: HydroRIVERS represents a vectorized line network of all global rivers that have a catchment area of at least 10 km² or an average river flow of at least 0.1 m³/sec, or both. HydroRIVERS has been extracted from the gridded HydroSHEDS core layers at 15 arc-second resolution. The global coverage of HydroRIVERS encompasses 8.5 million individual river reaches with an average length of 4.2 km, representing a total of 35.9 million km of rivers globally.

titre: MoWPP: Model of Within-host Pathogen Population dynamics
keywords: Within-host pathogen diversity, simulation model, genome evolution, kinetic model, virus evolution, diversity indices
abstract: MoWPP is a code that allows the user to run a model which simulates within-host genetic diversity across time under various demo-genetic assumptions, at the nucleotide resolution (i.e., the diversity is represented in terms of genetic sequences). Several viral kinetics are implemented. Several options for defining the fitness of genotypes are available. The code also allows the user to compute several diversity indices from the genetic sequences generated by the model, in particular the richness as well as the Shannon, Gini-Simpson and Jukes-Cantor diversity indices.

abstract: Environmental data (soil properties and land use) at sites of the RMQS program (French Soil Quality Monitoring Network). The French Soil Quality Monitoring Network (RMQS) is a national program for the assessment and long-term monitoring of the quality of French soils. This network is based on the monitoring of 2240 sites representative of French soils and their land use. These sites are spread over the whole French territory (metropolitan and overseas) along a systematic square grid of 16 km x 16 km cells. The network covers a broad spectrum of climatic, soil and land-use conditions (croplands, permanent grasslands, woodlands, orchards and vineyards, natural or scarcely anthropogenic land and urban parkland). The physical, chemical and biological properties of the soil are measured on each site. These soil analyses were carried out by the Soil Analysis Laboratory of INRAE (Arras, France). The spatial and temporal variability of soil properties are explained by biophysical variables, sources of contamination, history of land-use and management practices on each plot. Data contained via the provided link contains all the raw covariables used in the statistical analysis carried out by Karimi et al. (2018, Biogeography of soil bacteria and archaea across France. Science advances, 4(7), eaat1808, https://doi.org/10.1126/sciadv.aat1808).

abstract: The RPG data set is a geographical database used as a reference for the instruction of the aids of the common agricultural policy (CAP). The anonymized version that is distributed is part of the public service for providing reference data contains graphic data for plots (since 2015) and blocks (2014 and earlier editions), with their main culture. Anonymous RPG data are produced annualy and contain plots and blocks corresponding to those declared for campaign N in their known situation and approved by the administration, generally on 1 January of year N+1. These data cover the entire French territory (excluding Mayotte, including the overseas communities of Saint-Barthélemy and Saint-Martin).

abstract: This corpus is created as part of the BEYOND project. It contains 23 texts annotated for the Named Entity Recognition (NER) and Named Entity Normalisation (NEN) tasks. The annotated entities types are plants, pests, dates and places. The resources for the normalisation are the EPPO Global Database and the GeoNames geographical database. These texts were annotated using the BRAT annotation tool and, therefore, have the brat annotation format. Each annotation file name has a format file_id.ann. The texts cannot be redistributed due to their license terms and conditions. However, you will find the URL to their sources as well as more information about each text in the corpus description.docx file. English

abstract: Le fichier téléchargé contient 104 données sur la gravité de la pourriture brune de la pêche à la récolte pour différents lieux, cultivar et années. Chaque niveau de sévérité (Severity_score) est exprimé sur une échelle discrète de 0 à 3, pour des variétés de pêches qui se réfèrent à quatre cultivars virtuels ('early', 'mid-early', 'mid-late', 'late') définis sur la base de la durée de la saison de maturation des fruits (Vanalli et al., 2021, "Shifts in the thermal niche of fruit trees under climate change: The case of peach cultivation in France"). Le fichier est composé de trois feuilles : i) "Observations", c'est-à-dire les observations au sens propre, où sont indiqués le niveau de sévérité, la source, les auteurs, la variété, le lieu, l'année, et les données qui ont permis d'associer le niveau de sévérité ; ii) "Table_correspondance", qui indique comment une donnée, quantitative ou qualitative, a été passée à un niveau de sévérité dans l'échelle mentionnée ci-dessus : iii) légende, qui montre quelques informations relatives aux cultivars et à la construction de la feuille "observations".

abstract: ElasTetisearch is a software that enables the formulation of complex queries on data generated by the text-mining pipeline of BEYOND. The originality of this search engine is its ability to manipulate the data set's hierarchies (Taxonomy, Habitat Type, Relationship Type, Locations, …). An example of a possible query is to find all microorganisms present in the same habitats as Bacillus thuringiensis.

keywords: Fungal diversity, internal transcribed spacer, high-throughput sequencing, metabarcoding
abstract: GlobalFungi is a global database of fungal occurrences from high-throughput-sequencing metabarcoding studies. It contains billions of observations of fungal sequences from more than tens of thousands of samples with geographical locations and additional metadata. The database represents the most comprehensive atlas of global fungal distribution, and it is framed in such a way that third-party data addition is possible.

titre: Air mass trajectory and connectivity data
keywords: Spodoptera frugiperda, sugar beet, potyvirus, tropolink
abstract: Archive containing trajectory and connectivity data generated with tropolink for the preparation of the manuscript Richard et al. (2023, https://doi.org/10.1029/2023GH000885), as well as the corresponding specifications (node coordinates, dates and other tropolink options). The archive contains specifications, trajectories and connectivities for the three applications presented in the manuscript: (i) the study of airborne connectivity between areas of production of sugar beet, with starting altitude equal to 250m, 500m and 750m above ground level; (ii) the study of airborne connectivity between potyvirus populations; (iii) the study of invasion risk of Spodoptera frugiperda in Europe, North Africa and western Asia.

keywords: Webapp, Shiny, R, hosting service
abstract: The SK8 platform organizes the infrastructure and maintains a service offer for the hosting of R-Shiny web applications for users primarily working on INRAE topics. It is grounded on the R package "Shiny" which allows the user the production of interactive web applications without requiring advanced web development skills. This ease of development and access explains why Shiny applications are multiplying today in research units since they facilitate the sharing, promotion and democratization of scientific work.
